title: Admit validated model-proposed task hierarchies into guarded execution runtime
request: Begin the graph-admission package, staying focused on relevant tests and spending nothing on live models, preserving single holdout gate and deterministic fallback.
plan: Define an explicit double opt-in path for admitting validated model proposals into TaskDispatcher.
Enforce exact non-group leaf equality, transitive mandatory dependency preservation and bounded hierarchy rules.
Write comprehensive failing-before regressions covering admission, refusal, tampering and crash recovery for file and PostgreSQL backends.
Implement TaskDispatcher.admit and execution-time validation in TaskDispatcher._sources and SolutionTeam.
Subject the implementation to independent adversarial review, fix all confirmed defects, and verify zero regressions across all planning suites.

decisions.decision: Require double opt-in (enabled=True and admit_proposals=True) with a false default.
decisions.why: Model proposal admission must not activate task execution or alter deterministic runtime behaviour without explicit configuration.

decisions.decision: Enforce strict atomic leaf equality between proposed candidate and deterministic baseline.
decisions.why: The model is permitted to introduce grouping nodes and topological dependencies, but must never modify physical tasks, capabilities, scopes or acceptance checks.

decisions.decision: Record an immutable admission receipt containing candidate fingerprint, producer version and reference ID in state.
decisions.why: Checkpoint tampering or subsequent source changes must not silently replace or forge admitted graphs.

decisions.decision: Validate the reconstructed model graph inside adopt_sources before committing updated state.
decisions.why: Source updates must not leave dangling dependencies or invalid hierarchy trees in persistent checkpoints.

decisions.decision: Spend zero on live models during admission testing by using scripted boundaries and TP-02 compiler fixtures.
decisions.why: Integration boundaries must be fully verified and proved deterministic without consuming live model budgets.

change: Add opt-in model-proposed task graph admission to TaskDispatcher and SolutionTeam with structural leaf checks, hierarchy depth/node bounds, transitive dependency preservation, tamper-evident admission receipts, and re-grounding across source updates.

findings.defect: adopt_sources omitted validation of the reconstructed model graph against workflow rules.
findings.scenario: A source change on an admitted graph produces dangling or invalid dependencies which are written to state while claiming ready status.
findings.cause: adopt_sources re-grounded group edges onto updated leaves without validating the reconstructed candidate.
findings.fix: Validate the reconstructed graph against _validate_admitted_graph before updating checkpoint state, cleanly returning blocked on invalid structure.
findings.impact: A corrupted task graph would be durably committed and subsequently fail during dispatch.
alternatives: Revert to deterministic graph on source update

findings.defect: Unrooted group hierarchies and unparented leaves passed admission validation.
findings.scenario: A candidate graph with a disjoint orphan group or an unparented leaf node was admitted, breaking tree rendering in TaskPlan view.
findings.cause: _validate_admitted_graph only checked root.parent_id is None without asserting that all groups descend from root and all leaves have valid parents.
findings.fix: Assert that root is in transitive ancestors for all groups except root, and all leaf parent_ids belong to the group tree.
findings.impact: Disjoint groups and orphaned leaf nodes would be omitted from hierarchical task trees.

findings.defect: Unhandled Blocked exception escaped TaskDispatcher.admit on corrupted checkpoints.
findings.scenario: Calling admit on a project with a malformed task checkpoint crashed with an unhandled exception instead of returning a blocked result.
findings.cause: admit lacked an outer try-except Blocked block around project state inspection.
findings.fix: Wrap the turn block in try-except Blocked and return clean status blocked with the error message.
findings.impact: API callers would receive an unhandled 500 server error instead of a graceful refusal.

findings.defect: Checkpoint provenance tampering was undetected by _validate_admitted_graph.
findings.scenario: Altering reference_id or producer_version in a checkpoint was undetected because graph_fingerprint excludes provenance.
findings.cause: _validate_admitted_graph only checked fingerprint equality without verifying provenance fields against the admission record.
findings.fix: Verify that graph.provenance.method is model and reference_id and producer_version match state admission record.
findings.impact: Provenance records could be forged without invalidating graph fingerprint.
alternatives: Include provenance in graph_fingerprint (breaks schema fingerprint contract)

measurements.name: Task admission regression suite
measurements.gate: All 36 task admission tests must pass with zero skips across FileStore and PostgreSQL backends.
measurements.result: 36 tests passed in 22.2s with zero failures and zero skips.
limits: Covers admission and guarded execution; does not measure live-model generation quality.

measurements.name: Task planning full suite
measurements.gate: All 11 task planning test files must pass with zero regressions.
measurements.result: 357 tests across 11 test files passed in 46.8s with zero failures.
limits: Execution rollout remains disabled by default pending formal promotion gate rerun.

outcome: Model-proposed task graph admission is fully implemented and tested with 36 dedicated regressions across SQLite/file and PostgreSQL stores, 4 confirmed adversarial findings resolved, and all 357 planning tests passing with zero live model spend.
lessons: Reconstructed graphs in source update handlers must undergo full schema and contractual validation before saving.
Group hierarchies require explicit transitive root reachability assertions to prevent disjoint group forests.
When graph fingerprints exclude metadata fields like provenance, checkpoint receipts must explicitly verify those fields.
API-level dispatcher methods must catch internal domain exceptions and return structured blocked responses.
risks: Admitting model hierarchies could be confused with permission to enable default execution rollout.
Complex nested groups require strict depth limits to avoid UI rendering degradation.
